title: Rearrange the array in alternating positive and negative items
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Rearrange so signs alternate, starting with a positive number.
intuition: When positives and negatives are equal in count, their target slots are known up front: evens for positives, odds for negatives. No sorting or shifting is needed.

approaches.title: Brute: split into two lists then interleave
approaches.idea: Simple and clear, but O(n) extra memory.
approaches.code:
def rearrange_brute(a: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    pos = [x for x in a if x >= 0]
    neg = [x for x in a if x < 0]
    out = []
    for p, n in zip(pos, neg):
        out += [p, n]
    return out

approaches.title: Optimal (equal counts): direct index placement
approaches.whyWorks: Equal counts make the slot assignment a bijection.

approaches.title: Variant: unequal counts, keep relative order
approaches.idea: Interleave up to min(len) then append the leftovers.
approaches.code:
def rearrange_unequal(a: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    pos = [x for x in a if x >= 0]
    neg = [x for x in a if x < 0]
    out = []
    for i in range(min(len(pos), len(neg))):
        out += [pos[i], neg[i]]
    out += pos[min(len(pos), len(neg)):]
    out += neg[min(len(pos), len(neg)):]
    return out

edgeCases: Unequal counts of positives and negatives
Zeros — decide which side they belong to
commonMistakes: Assuming equal counts when the statement does not guarantee it
Breaking relative order when it is required
patternRecognition: Known target index formula -> direct placement beats any shifting loop
followUps: Do it in O(1) extra space
interviewInsight: Ask whether counts are equal and whether relative order matters — the two variants differ a lot.
